Fog Scout

When a match starts, Fog Scout reads the map name at the bottom left of the screen and puts the matching callout map on top of the game. After the round the map goes away again.

In the match

Text recognition runs on your PC. Map detection and the overlay open no internet connection.

Automatic callout maps
56 map pictures, layouts like Coal Tower II told apart, in a click-through window. See the six map styles →
Round timer and alerts
A timer below the map while the round runs, the search time while you wait, and a sound when the lobby is found or your bloodpoints stop going up at the cap.
Score tracker
Counts the score events at the top right while you play and adds up each category: as rings, bars or one line next to the map. A full category shows MAX.
Teammates' loadouts
As a survivor, press Esc once in the match: Fog Scout reads the other survivors' perks, item, add-ons and offering from the pause menu and shows them next to each of them. Optional.
Cards around the game
Next to the map, optional cards show system values, today's rounds and the music that is playing. Arrange them in the overlay editor, one layout per screen size.
Keys and controller on screen
Optional: shows which movement keys, mouse buttons and controller buttons you hold. With a recording, they are saved next to the video and shown again in the clip editor.
Notes per map and killer
A short note of your own for each map and each killer, shown on the map card in the round.
112/112map pictures in English and German, 720p to 4K and ultrawide, all correct
0false alarms on 319 screens without a banner
≈0.1 sper picture at 1440p
0of 120 unknown map names assigned to a wrong map

Tested with real screenshots and rebuilt banners on real game backgrounds. Synthetic tests do not replace a real round.

Recordings and clips

Recording with OBS
Starts and labels recordings per match, with a clip editor for the highlights. Each mark you set in a round can become a clip of its own, and Fog Scout shows how many more rounds fit on the drive.
Clip editor
Cut, hide names, add subtitles, music and your own voice, join clips from several rounds or make a vertical short.
Moments
Finds quiet stretches and dark loading screens in a recording and offers to cut them out.
Steam screenshots
Your F12 screenshots in one gallery: crop, draw on them and hide names. Fog Scout saves an edited copy and never touches the original.
YouTube upload
Optional: uploads a round or a clip to your channel and pauses while you are in a lobby.

Statistics

Match statistics
Role, killer, kills, escapes and bloodpoints per round, your form by weekday and time of day, perk pairs and waiting times. Kept on your PC.
Records and sessions
Streaks, your best week and every session, with a short summary when you close DBD.
Bloodpoints and farming
Bloodpoints per hour, and farming rounds counted apart or hidden with one switch.
Export
Rounds as a CSV file, filtered by period, role, killer or map.

Tools

Server region
Choose which regions you connect to and see the game server you are on.
Perk calculator
Combine perks, items and add-ons for up to four survivors and a killer, and see what they give after diminishing returns, skill checks included.
Discord and Spotify
Optional: show map and role as Discord status, see your Spotify queue.
Search everything
Ctrl+F finds every page, setting, map and round.
Ask Claude
Optional, with your own API key: questions about your statistics and suggestions in the clip editor. Only figures and fixed texts are sent, never player names.
Detects the game language
Map names in English, German, French, Spanish, Italian, Polish, Portuguese, Turkish, Russian, Chinese, Japanese and Korean. Fog Scout spots the game language by itself.
Seven languages
The app in German, English, Italian, Russian, Chinese, Japanese and Korean. Follows the Windows language, switchable in the settings.
Safe updates and backups
Updates come from the GitHub release and are checked against a SHA-256 before they install. Settings and rounds go into one backup file.

Inside the app

The control window, filled with made-up rounds.

Built to stay out of the game

Both tools were designed around one rule: do not interact with Dead by Daylight. They are still unofficial. Behaviour Interactive has not approved map overlays or region tools, so you use them at your own risk.

  • ReadsScreen pixels, the way OBS or Discord screen sharing does, and window information.
  • NeverKeyboard or mouse input to the game, or any automation of game actions.
  • NeverAccess to the game process: no memory reading, no injection.
  • NeverReading or changing game files.
  • NeverHidden information. The callout map is a static community map, with no generators or positions. Teammates' loadouts come from the pause menu, where the game shows them to you.
  • ChangesOnly if you use the server region feature: the Windows hosts file, which "Allow all" puts back.
